needs: Record daily habits quickly on phone and desktop with repeated timed events.
Associate a tracking day and its after-midnight events with the appropriate following main night.
Export collected data for later comparison with Garmin outside the MVP.
context: Green tea, black tea, mate, activity details/durations/times, meals, alcohol, gluten, naps, late sugar, evening hot drinks, cat presence, before/after-night stress and early waking are explicitly requested.
Repository setup and development-ready planning are authorized; application implementation and production deployment are not part of this task.
Product questions in docs/mvp-questions.md remain open. Proposed defaults are not user-approved decisions; resolve the relevant questions before implementing dependent behavior.
Proposed stack: React/TypeScript, FastAPI and SQLite with Docker; existing hosting uses a shared HTTPS reverse proxy.
Public source repository; personal data and Garmin exports must remain private.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Deliver an authenticated French mobile-first installable PWA with server-persisted records shared across phone and desktop sessions; expose connectivity and save failures without claiming unsaved changes were saved.

AC2: Preserve actual timestamps and timezone alongside a tracking-day date and stable editable main-night association; demonstrate after-midnight, boundary, DST and manual reassignment examples using the confirmed assignment rule.

AC3: Support repeated beverage intakes with time and distinct green tea, black tea and mate categories; support the confirmed meaning of combinations and represent evening hot drinks without double counting.
AC4: Support repeated physical activity sessions with activity details, start time and duration, and repeated naps with time and duration; validate interval and duration consistency.
AC5: Capture meal timing, alcohol, gluten and late sugar using explicit present/absent/unknown states and the confirmed event-versus-daily granularity; preserve the meaning of late sugar in exports.

AC6: Capture cat presence for a night, stress for the confirmed before/after periods, and early-waking context with confirmed planned/actual semantics; identify the assessed date/period unambiguously.
AC7: Provide a day/night history with create, edit and delete operations; preserve repeated entries and distinguish missing data, explicit absence and completed daily assessments.

AC8: Export all user-collected data in versioned JSON and a documented normalized CSV bundle, including IDs, timezone/offset, original timestamps, units, missingness, tracking days and night links; verify completeness using synthetic round-trip fixtures.

AC9: Keep Garmin imports/synchronization, credentials, correlation calculations and health recommendations out of the MVP; document the export join convention for future Garmin records without inventing Garmin values.

AC10: Provide reproducible local startup, a container deployment artifact, persistent storage and documented backup/restore; verify authentication and isolation of private data, and commit synthetic data only; do not deploy production as part of planning.

product.title: SommeilEnOr personal sleep context journal
product.overview: A fast French PWA to collect daily and nightly context and export it for later sleep analysis.
goals: Low-friction repeated event capture and daily recap.
Reliable temporal links across midnight and devices.
Complete portable records with explicit missingness.
non_goals: Correlation dashboards, causal claims or health recommendations.
Production deployment during initial corpus creation.

backlog_items.title: Define tracking days nights and collection data contracts
problem: Midnight and ambiguous missing values can make future sleep comparisons incorrect.
scope_in: Resolve questions 4, 5, 9, 10, 14 and 15 in docs/mvp-questions.md before finalizing affected contracts.
Define event, component, tracking day, main night, assessment, stable ID, unit, schema version and tri-state answer contracts.
Store actual timestamps independently from editable night association; distinguish naps from the main night.
Priority rationale: temporal identity and missingness are dependencies of every capture screen.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Document the agreed assignment rule with 00:30 and 08:00 examples, boundary values, DST and late bedtime/manual override cases.
AC2: Define unique daily stress assessment ownership and unambiguous before/after-night references.
AC3: Define unknown/none/not-applicable/completed semantics and a migration-safe export schema.

backlog_items.title: Build authenticated cross-device PWA foundation
problem: A public repository must deliver a private journal usable across devices.
scope_in: Confirm access model, offline scope and stack (questions 1, 2, 22).
French responsive app shell, install manifest and production service worker/update behavior.
Authenticated API, server persistence, closed registration default proposal, sessions and appropriate mutation protection.
Visible save/connectivity states; offline writes only if explicitly selected and designed.
Priority rationale: access control and reliable persistence precede personal-data collection.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Verify unauthenticated users cannot read, mutate or export journal data.
AC2: Demonstrate a saved record is visible on a second authenticated browser and layouts work on mobile and desktop.
AC3: Verify installability over HTTPS, update behavior and truthful handling of failed/offline saves.

backlog_items.title: Collect repeated beverages physical activities and naps
problem: Repeated daily events cannot be represented by one boolean per category.
scope_in: Resolve beverage combinations, quantity units and exercise options (questions 6–8, 11–12).
Quick creation and recap editing of distinct beverage intakes, activity sessions and naps.
Retain multiple entries on the same day, event times/durations and editable night links.
Priority rationale: timed repeated events are the core collection workflow.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Save two green teas, one black tea and one mate at distinct times without overwriting any intake; exercise the agreed combination representation.
AC2: Create multiple physical activities and naps; reject invalid intervals/durations and allow corrections.
AC3: Represent evening hot drinks consistently with existing beverage records, with no duplicate event.

backlog_items.title: Collect meal night context and daily assessments
problem: Meal and night context needs clear granularity and meaningful unanswered states.
scope_in: Resolve meal granularity, sugar threshold, cat context, stress periods and early-wake fields (questions 9–16).
Capture meal times, alcohol/gluten, late sugar, night cat presence and stress assessments.
Separate planned early wake constraints from observed awakenings if both are selected.
Optional subjective sleep fields only after confirmation.
Priority rationale: complete the requested factor set after shared capture patterns exist.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Save and edit all requested factors while distinguishing unanswered values from explicit negative answers.
AC2: Display the exact assessed day or period for each stress answer on both sides of a night, with no contradictory duplicates.
AC3: Verify early-wake and late-sugar exports preserve the confirmed meaning, including time and reason where selected.

backlog_items.title: Deliver day night history and portable exports
problem: The collection MVP must already produce reliable inputs for later external comparisons.
scope_in: Day/night navigation, historical editing, deletion and completion state.
Versioned complete JSON plus normalized CSV bundle and data dictionary.
All repeated events, components, daily assessments and associations included.
Document future Garmin alignment by wake date and actual timezone; no integration implemented.
Priority rationale: useful history and lossless export complete the collection promise.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Export a synthetic journal spanning midnight and DST, repeated events and missing/negative answers; compare every exported entity and relationship to persisted data.
AC2: Demonstrate historical time edits and night overrides remain consistent in history and export.
AC3: Ensure exports are authenticated, omit secrets, and contain no fabricated Garmin or correlation fields.

backlog_items.title: Package and verify collection MVP for self hosting
problem: A cross-device journal needs reproducible operations and recoverable persistent storage.
scope_in: Document local startup and selected dependency versions, container build and generic HTTPS reverse-proxy integration.
Use environment templates without real deployment addresses or credentials.
Document and exercise backup/restore with synthetic data and persistent volumes.
Focused integration and responsive-browser checks; French i18n contract validation.
Priority rationale: operational verification is required before any later deployment.
scope_out: Garmin integration, correlations and production deployment.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Start a clean instance from documented commands and verify a restart preserves synthetic journal entries.
AC2: Restore a synthetic backup into an isolated instance and compare records and exported links.
AC3: Run the relevant automated checks and mobile/desktop smoke checks; record evidence without claiming production deployment.

orchestration_task.title: Orchestrate SommeilEnOr collection MVP delivery
plan: Resolve the product decisions required by each slice with the user; update acceptance criteria through the Logics workflow before dependent implementation.
Deliver High-priority temporal/data contracts first, then authenticated PWA foundation.
Deliver High-priority repeated events, meal/night assessments, then history and full export.
Deliver Medium-priority packaging and restore verification after the functional slices.
Record evidence against each request AC, run appropriate checks and Logics validation, and close out only after actual implementation; deployment needs a separate instruction.
